texts.title: When does failure teach?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall the last mistake you made… and keep it in mind.
texts.hook.h2: They say: failure is the first step to success… really?
texts.hook.h3: I gave the same presentation twice… and made the same mistake.
texts.hook.h4: 53 studies asked: hear the explanation first… or try before it?
texts.hook.h5.frame: Ask why… or just move on?
texts.hook.h5: When something doesn't work… do you ask why? Or just move on?
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour. Her presentation didn't work.
texts.s1.l1: No big deal… failure is the first step to success!
texts.s1.l2: What will you do with the presentation?
texts.s1.l3: I'll present it again, just as it is.
texts.s1.a2: And you… did you find where your mistake was?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time Nour asks.
texts.s1.l4: What will you do with the presentation?
texts.s1.l5: First… what do you think didn't work?
texts.s1.l6: Too many numbers… I got lost myself.
texts.s1.l7: One idea per slide… not perfect, but clearer.
texts.book.card: To get better you must fail… there's no other way.
texts.book.l1: The book says: behind any improvement are lots of small falls.
texts.book.l2: And someone better than you at something? Chances are, they failed more than you.
texts.verdict.card: 53 studies · those who tried before the explanation understood better
texts.verdict.nuance: But someone who tries alone all the way, with no one to clarify? Often learns less.
texts.verdict.l2: 53 studies: students tried before the explanation, most couldn't… and after it, understood better than those taught first.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Nour: before trying again, ask someone who saw your work. It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone repeating the same thing… expecting a new result.
